## Why This Is Asked
This question explores a dynamic sequence with range-frequency queries, introducing a new angle not covered by the existing questions. It teaches augmenting a balanced tree and split/merge techniques for range queries.

## Key Concepts
- Implicit treap
- Subtree frequency arrays
- Range queries via split/merge
- Amortized O(log n) updates

## Code Example
```javascript
class Node { constructor(chIndex){ this.chIndex=chIndex; this.pri=Math.random(); this.left=null; this.right=null; this.size=1; this.freq=new Array(26).fill(0); this.freq[chIndex]=1; } }
function upd(t){ if(!t) return; t.size=1; t.freq.fill(0); if(t.left){ t.size+=t.left.size; for(let i=0;i<26;i++) t.freq[i]+=t.left.freq[i]; } if(t.right){ t.size+=t.right.size; for(let i=0;i<26;i++) t.freq[i]+=t.right.freq[i]; } t.freq[t.chIndex]+=1; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to larger alphabets efficiently?
- How would you test correctness with random operations and a naive baseline?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates knowledge of persistent data structures, rope-based string representations, and efficient substring hashing under versioning—skills directly applicable to building collaborative text editors.

## Key Concepts
- **Persistent data structures with path-copying**: Each modification creates new nodes along the affected path while sharing unchanged subtrees with previous versions
- **Rope implementation**: Balanced BST enabling O(log n) split and concatenate operations
- **Subtree aggregates**: Cached length and rolling hash enable O(log n) substring queries
- **Memory considerations**: Path-copying creates O(log n) new nodes per edit; total memory grows proportionally with edit count, though unused nodes can be garbage collected
- **Collision handling**: Use a polynomial rolling hash with large prime modulus; combine with second hash function (e.g., MD5 or SHA prefix) for verification in critical applications
- **Balancing and concatenation**: Treap balancing (via randomized priorities) maintains O(log n) operations; concatenation merges two trees by attaching the smaller as a child of the larger, or by creating a new root with both as children

## Why This Is Asked
Designing a small string-structure task that still demonstrates practical data-structure thinking.

- How would you optimize memory by pruning zero-count branches?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates your ability to combine two simple data structures into a practical, efficient solution. It tests understanding of amortized analysis, edge-case handling, and how to track auxiliary information (min values) alongside primary data.

## Key Concepts

- **Deque semantics**: Two-ended insertion and deletion require symmetric handling of both ends.
- **Two-stack technique**: By transferring elements between stacks, two LIFOs can simulate FIFO queue behavior.
- **Local mins per stack**: Each element stores the minimum value present in its stack at insertion time, allowing O(1) minimum queries across both stacks.
